brief: Defend the unfashionable position that most professional skill is learned by copying, not by creativity. Must engage: (1) how musicians, painters, and lawyers actually train; (2) the modern anxiety that imitation is theft or stagnation; (3) where copying genuinely fails and originality earns its keep. One personal-feeling anecdote allowed, invented details fine, but it must do argumentative work. End on the relationship between copying and voice.
